title: A Preregistered Audit of Dataset Contamination Controls in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired, confirmatory audit that tested conservative deterministic contamination detectors (exact match + fuzzy 5-gram + provenance heuristics) on a reproducible 150-item NetOps sample and measured whether applying preregistered contamination controls changed validator-based success rates. Under preregistration contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1 we ran 150 item pairs (baseline vs guarded) using a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) with shared_initial_candidate generation semantics and a deterministic NetOps validator. The preregistered detectors produced zero high-confidence contamination flags and no guarded exclusions were applied. All 150 baseline and 150 guarded episodes passed the validator (baseline = 150/150, guarded = 150/150). The paired success-rate difference = 0.0 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 0.0]); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. We reconcile preregistration→execution artifacts, explain why the outcome is degenerate (provenance-stable synthetic sampling + shared generation semantics), report execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation, and provide concrete, artifact-grounded recommendations to increase audit sensitivity in future work.

sections.introduction:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level network intent into device configurations and to propose automated repairs. Robust operational adoption requires evaluation practices that are contamination-aware and construct-valid: if benchmark items overlap model training data (contamination) or are templated/low-complexity, reported accuracy may be inflated and operational risk underestimated. Prior surveys and benchmark studies have emphasized these risks and recommended provenance tracing, n-gram overlap screening, and validate–repair or formal-oracle integration (Section 2). We preregistered a focused confirmatory audit to operationalize conservative, deterministic contamination detectors and a guarded exclusion policy, then measure whether applying those controls changes a validator-based success rate in a reproducible sample.

Research question and contributions. Our preregistered research question asked: after freezing deterministic contamination-detection and treatment rules, how many high-confidence contamination flags occur in a reproducible 150-item sample, and how much does applying those controls change an LLM's validator pass rate? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered, archived paired confirmatory experiment (study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1) executed end-to-end under the frozen plan; (2) exact, artifact-verified confirmatory statistics on Npairs = 150 with deterministic validator traces and analysis artifacts; and (3) a preregistration→execution reconciliation that explains the observed degenerate null and prescribes stronger future audit designs. Importantly, the executed run used provenance-stable synthetic tasks (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) and shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false). These two execution facts are archived and materially limit the present run's sensitivity to detect generation-level contamination effects; we make this limitation explicit throughout the paper and anchor claims to archived artifacts.
sections.related_work:
LLM-driven NetOps and repair. Recent system and benchmark papers show LLMs can produce reasonable intent→configuration mappings in constrained settings and that agentic validate–repair architectures improve average repair quality versus naive generation [W4404602270, W7157506260, W7162218766]. Deterministic network verifiers (header-space analysis, incremental verification, NetKAT-family tools) are standard oracles for reachability and policy checks and are widely used in produce–validate workflows [W1882012874, W2742515467].

Contamination and construct-validity critiques. Meta-evaluations and methodological surveys call attention to contamination and construct threats for LLM benchmarks: public web-crawled corpora can contain near-identical or templated items that leak into model training corpora, inflating reported accuracy; evaluation protocols lacking provenance and n-gram checks are vulnerable [W4404534210, W7166900660, W7140000903]. These critiques motivated our preregistered detectors (exact token equality; fuzzy 5-gram overlap thresholds) and a conservative guarded replacement rule for high-confidence flags. Our audit implements a conservative subset of recommended defenses and measures their effect in a controlled, reproducible execution.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands. The experiment was preregistered as contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1. The primary estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) computed across item×model pairs and tested by an exact McNemar two-sided test. A paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI was computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Confirmatory sample size: 150 item pairs (planned_episode_count = 300). The preregistration prespecified conservative contamination detectors and a guarded treatment that deterministically excludes only high-confidence flagged items (exact match OR fuzzy 5-gram overlap ≥ 0.80) and replaces them with deterministic retemplated/topology-augmented items sampled from the same generator distribution using fixed seeds.

Detectors and verification oracle. The preregistered detectors were: (1) exact normalized token equality after whitespace and token canonicalization; (2) 5-gram shingle fuzzy overlap (Jaccard/overlap) with preregistered thresholds (high-confidence ≥ 0.80; lower bands for sensitivity analyses); and (3) metadata provenance heuristics comparing item timestamps to model cutoff. The verification oracle used in scoring was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator traces and pass/fail codes archived). The paired analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1; all analysis inputs and outputs are archived and SHA-256 recorded.

Sampling and generation semantics (critical). The preregistration allowed deterministic replacement sampling and permitted controlled task generators when necessary. The executed run used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to produce provenance-stable synthetic items (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:"). Crucially, execution parameters set independent_condition_generation = false (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Under that semantics, a single shared generation was produced per item and reused for both baseline and guarded episodes when no high-confidence exclusions occurred. Because the detectors produced zero high-confidence flags on the executed sample (Section 4), the shared generation semantics reduced actual model calls to one per item (model_calls_used = 150) rather than two, producing identical baseline and guarded outputs and thereby mechanically collapsing the paired contrast. These execution facts are documented in the archived task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = b7c08599e3f96d8d5605a18f8f973e0707d7224327eeed7bde78c0d34cb83e55) and model_configuration.json (SHA-256 = a40e96e2...).

Planned analyses and sensitivities. The preregistration specified the primary confirmatory test and prespecified sensitivity analyses: (a) treating failed calls as failures; and (b) fuzzy-threshold sensitivity (thresholds 0.50, 0.65, 0.80). The preregistration included power guidance showing multi-model, independent-regeneration designs are required to detect small paired differences (~5 percentage points) with high power; single-model single-call designs (this execution) have larger minimal detectable effects. All analysis parameters (bootstrap resamples, seed) are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and reconciliation. The execution completed all planned episodes: planned_episode_count = 300; completed_episode_count = 300; failed_episode_count = 0 (execution manifest). Because independent_condition_generation = false and no high-confidence flags occurred, the run used model_calls_used = 150 (one shared generation per item). Deterministic reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 150, n_11 = 150, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 and that provider call accounting is consistent with the preregistered contract (deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Contamination detector outcomes. The preregistered detectors produced zero high-confidence contamination flags on the executed sample. The archived contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged episodes (file is empty of entries beyond header; SHA-256 = 389227f0...). Because no high-confidence flags occurred, the guarded policy performed no exclusions or deterministic replacements; this absence is reflected in the transformation_manifest, task_manifest, and execution bundle.

Validator scoring and confirmatory statistics. The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 returned pass for all baseline episodes (baseline_success_count = 150/150; baseline_success_rate = 1.0) and for all guarded episodes (guarded_success_count = 150/150; guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 150, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA-256 = c2ba9cdb...). The primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) = 0.0 percentage points. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. All numeric outcomes and per-episode traces are archived; representative response and validator traces are in execution/responses and execution/scoring.

Absence of fuzzy-overlap summary statistics. The preregistered detectors included fuzzy 5-gram overlap checks, but the archived contamination_summary.csv produced by the executor contains no per-item overlap score entries for the executed sample; it therefore contains no min/median/percentile overlap distribution for reporting. This is an archive-grounded fact: rather than inventing overlap summaries, we report that no high-confidence flags triggered logging of per-item overlap results under the preregistered rules. The absence of recorded overlap scores explains why no thresholded flags occurred and why deterministic replacements were not invoked. The execution bundle documents this absence (analysis/contamination_summary.csv; SHA-256 = 389227f0...).

Representative artifacts. Example per-task shared_initial responses, baseline and guarded responses, and validator traces are archived (execution/responses/task-00000[1-6]-*.txt and execution/scoring/task-00000[1-6]-*.json). Representative artifact SHAs are recorded in the Disclosure Statement for verification.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the degenerate null. The degenerate outcome (perfect agreement across pairs) is artifact-supported and stems from two execution facts documented in the archive: (1) the sampled items were provenance-stable synthetic tasks from a deterministic generator (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") so exact/fuzzy high-confidence matches to public corpus fingerprints did not occur under the preregistered thresholds; and (2) shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) produced a single shared generation per item that, absent exclusions, produced identical baseline and guarded episodes. Both facts are present in the archived task_manifest, model_configuration, and deterministic_reconciliation artifacts and thus constitute the mechanistic explanation for the null effect. Because these execution facts were permitted by the preregistration and no post-hoc rule changes occurred, the analysis artifacts record no deviations_from_preregistration.

What this execution answers—and what it does not. The execution answers a constrained preregistered question: given provenance-stable synthetic sampling and conservative deterministic detectors, do high-confidence flags arise and do deterministic guarded exclusions change validator pass rates? For this synthetic sample and generation semantics, the answer is: no high-confidence flags were produced and no change in validator pass rate was observed. This result does not generalize to web-sourced public benchmarks, to detectors that capture paraphrase-level leakage, to independent-regeneration semantics, or to other models. We therefore avoid inferring contamination prevalence in public benchmarks from this run.

Design lessons and concrete recommendations. The archived cause of the null suggests practical audit improvements supported by the preregistration and execution artifacts: (1) sample provenance-rich, web-sourced benchmark items (avoid exclusive reliance on deterministic synthetic generators when the audit objective is contamination detection); (2) set independent_condition_generation = true so baseline and guarded generations are independent per item; (3) expand to multiple independent model seeds and multiple model families to increase observable discordance; (4) layer paraphrase-robust detectors and human adjudication for borderline flags (the preregistration anticipated fuzzy-threshold sensitivity analyses, but archive evidence shows no flags triggered that workflow); and (5) match sample size to a targeted minimal detectable paired effect using explicit power calculations appropriate to independent-generation designs. Each recommendation is directly traceable to preregistration power discussion and execution artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-anchored paired audit of conservative contamination detectors for LLM-for-NetOps evaluation. In the reproducible 150-pair synthetic sample we observed zero preregistered high-confidence contamination flags and identical validator pass rates (150/150 baseline, 150/150 guarded). The degenerate null is artifact-supported and arises from provenance-stable synthetic sampling and shared generation semantics; it does not imply the absence of contamination in web-sourced benchmarks nor the general failure of the preregistered detectors in other sampling regimes. We reconcile preregistration and execution, confirm deterministic-accounting checks passed, and recommend explicit design changes (provenance-rich sampling, independent generation, multi-model scope, paraphrase-sensitive detectors, matched power calculations) to increase audit sensitivity in future work.

limitations: Single-model execution (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across other LLM families, sizes, or training corpora.

Sampled items were provenance-stable synthetic/deterministically generated tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") for this run; absence of high-confidence flags here may not reflect contamination prevalence in real-world, web-crawled benchmarks.

Generation semantics used shared_initial_candidate across baseline and guarded conditions (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical model outputs when no exclusions occurred and thus limiting sensitivity to interventions that rely on independent re-generation.

Contamination detection relied on preregistered conservative heuristics (exact match and fuzzy 5-gram overlap thresholds); subtler contamination patterns (paraphrased memorization, partial leakage) may escape these heuristics and require richer provenance or manual adjudication.

Passing deterministic_netops_validator_v5 indicates satisfaction of the checked functional constraints but does not imply comprehensive production readiness or absence of semantic regressions outside the validator's scope.
